tiers.S: Previous submissions: every registry raster that carries an operator-claimed leaderboard score (ledger/claimed_scores_20261024.csv). This is the operator's own first-sentence definition of 'unique': do not copy a previous submission.
tiers.L: Lane witnesses: every distinct registry raster whose 3 px halo covers < 50 % of the footprint (860 non-empty rasters at the 2026-10-24 scan; 861 counting one empty file).
tiers.T: Literal rule: ALL distinct registry rasters, including blankets whose halo covers >= 50 % of the footprint and dense surfaces. Structurally unsatisfiable: the 17GEMSDOE E-proba surface is positive on 100 % of the footprint, so every nonempty candidate has forward overlap 1.0.

rationale: Thresholds (0.90 / 0.70 / 3 px) are NOT changed. What differs between tiers is only WHICH registry rasters the test is applied to. Tier T cannot be passed by any candidate (certificate: evidence/lcs_registry_final.json -> blankets, plus 17GEMSDOE E-proba), and Tier L cannot be passed together with high consensus quality (price-of-uniqueness frontier in evidence/lcs_build.json). Tier S is the reading under which 'unique submission' is both decidable and meaningful.
decided_by: autonomous session 2026-10-24 (operator asked for no manual input); previous sessions left the deadlock unresolved and every candidate ended 'negative'.
operator_override: Set decisive_tier to "L" or "T" and run `make site` (or `python scripts/check_site.py`): the homepage verdict, audit receipt and CI will follow the new tier. All three tiers are always measured and displayed regardless of this setting.
never: silently drop a raster from the comparison
describe a MODEL projection as a score
